chunk_findings.detail: `on_refutation` still returns None for a gate whose recorded outcome is `passed`. The docstring in the same function defines None as “passed by a clean review, or not passed”, so a caller that only adds the “ON REFUTATION” suffix when this returns a dict now renders a plain pass. Input: `gates[gate].outcome == "passed"`, `evidence["passed_on_refutation"] == {"confirmed": 0}`, and `triage_counts` reports `confirmed == 1` (the B31e91454f8 state, including a status read that does not re-enter triage). The new branch returns None while the record stays passed, so the gate still shows passed — and the refutation flag that made the bad pass visible is suppressed. Revocation lives only in `_revoke_refutation_pass`, which this read path never calls, and the new regression test never calls `on_refutation`.

chunk_findings.detail: `attest` treats a question as multiple-choice with `if row["options"]`, but the same change’s `payload` treats a missing options key as free text (`row.get("options") or []`). A free-text question row that only has `type == QUESTION` and `text` (no `options` key — the case this bug is about) raises KeyError on `row["options"]` before `E.answer`, so `ddflow approvals attest <id>` never records the transcript answer. `verify` already uses `row.get("options")` and would check `row["answer"]`; only the write path crashes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:476

chunk_findings.detail: The change does not actually fix the `approvals_answer` surface for question asks. A question ask has an empty `verb`, but `approvals_answer` still contains its original `row is None or not row["verb"]` guard and returns `no approval request <id>` before a free-text answer can be recorded. The only hunk in this file filters questions out of the `all_pending` branch of the separate approve path, so for input `ddflow approvals answer <question-id> "text"` on a waiting question, the question still remains unanswered. This preserves the exact bug the change claims to fix, and the listed regression tests do not exercise `approvals_answer`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/approvals_answer.py:approvals_answer

chunk_findings.detail: For a question ask (`row["type"] == E.QUESTION`), `payload` returns an AskUserQuestion payload with `"options": []`. AskUserQuestion is a multiple-choice tool: the only way a person can answer is by selecting one of the provided options. With zero options there is no selectable answer and no free-text input field, so the person cannot provide the free-text answer this branch claims to support. This means the `ddflow approvals ask <id>` surface for a question ask still has no usable answer path, defeating the fix for B-question-ask-unreachable. The input is any ask with `type == E.QUESTION`; when the harness sends this payload to the person, the client rejects it or presents nothing to choose, and the question remains unanswerable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:154-165 (`payload`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new brief text instructs the operator to answer a pending question with `ddflow approvals ask ID`. That is the ask-creation command, not the answer path for an existing ask; the answer command in this change is `ddflow approvals answer` (the companion file `ddflow/api/approvals_answer.py` is the route being modified to reach `engine.answer`). Given a pending question, an operator following the emitted brief will run `ddflow approvals ask <qid>` and create/attempt to create a new ask instead of answering the question, so the surface still does not tell the person how to answer it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/view.py pending_line

chunk_findings.detail: `payload` builds a question's AskUserQuestion options as `[{"label": str(o)}]` and never sets `description`. The same function's approval branch always emits `{label, description}` because that is the tool input the agent must send unaltered (2–4 options, each requiring both fields). Given a question whose `options` are `["ship it", "hold"]`, the payload is `{"questions":[{"question":...,"header":"Question","multiSelect":false,"options":[{"label":"ship it"},{"label":"hold"}]}]}`. The tool rejects that input, so a preset-option question still never appears for a person to answer.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:164

data.probe: Fixed: each preset option now emits both label and description (answer the question with this option), matching the approval branch shape. test asserts all descriptions non-empty.

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier KeyError is still in the new `attest` branch: `if row["options"]:` raises when a question row has `type == QUESTION` and `text` but no `options` key — the free-text case this bug is about. `payload` and `verify` already treat a missing key as free text via `row.get("options")`, so `ddflow approvals attest <id>` dies before `E.answer` and never records the transcript answer. An empty list would fall through; only a missing key fails.
